column1: # Player-facing settings: the iOS launcher (dm/ios/Sources/Launcher.swift) and the Mac app's settings window (dm/mac/Launcher.swift) show them before the game starts; Mac front ends read the same list.

# dm/games/settings.py writes one game's list into its app (dm/launcher.json; build_ipa.sh, and dm/mac/pack_app.py through the NSP script): the rows whose condition holds for that game, with its defaults. Each sets an environment variable the host reads when the game starts; one an env file sets

# (Documents/env.txt, the bundle's dm/env.txt) is shown but kept. Heavy diagnostics stay environment-only; the bounded performance trace is an explicit opt-in setting. The player's page is docs/settings.md.
#   variable  the environment variable the setting sets
#   kind      choice: values value=label,... (languages: the game's own, from its control data); range: values low:high:step, shown as a percentage;
#             toggle: values - (on sets 1, off 0) or <on>/<off>, the two values the variable takes (on/off)
#   default   a value (a toggle's: 1 on, 0 off); DM_GAME_<NAME>: the host's own default from the game profile (game_profile.h, game.py); build:<VAR>: the IPA build's setting (build_ipa.sh)
#             <ios>|<mac> selects the platform's default before resolving a profile macro or build variable

#   shown     always; DM_GAME_<NAME>!=<value> or ==<value>; fixups:<KEY>: main's rewriter table has that key (a stub in the game's build, patch_nso.py); languages>1; gfxapi:<API>: the packer's GFXAPI;
#             platform:<ios | mac>: the app's platform (SETTINGS_PLATFORM, ios when unset), for a switch only that platform's front end reads
#   section   Game, Controls or Performance: a heading on the single settings screen. Rows appear in table order within each section
#             Reset to tested defaults clears all launcher choices; values fixed by an env file stay
#   label, note  the setting's name and the line under it (may be empty; only for a setting with a cost: latency, memory, heat)
#   meta      optional, key=value pairs separated by ; (settings.py META lists the keys; docs/frontends.md, The settings list, describes them):
#             level=basic  a setting a front end shows first;  needs=<VAR>=<value>  a sub-setting, drawn only while the row that sets <VAR> has that value

column8: The game may hold a lower rate under load to preserve game speed.
Adjusts resolution between 70% and 100% under load. Turn off to keep full resolution for the selected console mode.
Prevents the game's own dynamic resolution from going below the selected scale. Automatic quality owns the scale while enabled.
Adjusts live quality toward the FPS target; cannot guarantee an unreachable target.

Clips distant geometry after reaching the resolution floor; does not change actor traversal.
A far-clip limit; not a universal object or terrain LOD control.
Limits eligible trilinear anisotropic samplers. Preserves guest LOD, depth, reduction and low-anisotropy data sampling; keeps texture allocations.
Uses a matching prepared pulling pipeline while its native layout loads. Falls back to the full search when unavailable; may briefly increase vertex work.
Uses more GPU time and can increase heat.
Uses generated game fonts and layouts; follows physical button positions. Applies next launch.
Up to one frame more display latency.
Keeps a pipeline archive; uses more memory.
Builds every shader pair; can use hundreds of MB. Keep off on A16 unless memory measurements allow it.
Writes bounded stutter.jsonl and capabilities.json in Documents. Restart after changing; measure recording overhead in A/B tests.
Conservative default: compare 1/2/4 on the same route. More workers can increase heat and frame spikes.
Reuses verified texture conversions; up to 256 MB on disk and one 16 MB temporary write.
Applies before gameplay; the learned and bundled shader lists remain enabled.
Before gameplay uses the selected worker count and adds an initial wait.
Lower output uses smaller presentation buffers. Internal render scale is a separate setting.
Prepares a bounded list from previous sessions, while at least 512 MB of memory headroom remains.
Higher budgets can reduce repeat compilation stalls but keep more pipelines in memory.
